data.name: Warn_ThrottleChannel
data.value: ArduPilot maps Hobbywing ESCs by throttle channel (= motor output number). A wrong channel makes this ESC follow another motor's throttle.

data.name: Warn_NodeId
data.value: The ESC will answer on the new node ID and show up as a new row; the old row goes stale. Some ESCs need a power cycle.

data.name: Warn_ThrottlePwm
data.value: With PWM the ESC ignores DroneCAN throttle from ArduPilot and only follows the PWM signal wire. The motor will not respond to the flight controller over CAN.

data.name: Warn_ThrottleCan
data.value: The ESC will take throttle from DroneCAN (ArduPilot) again.

data.name: Warn_CanBaud
data.value: The ESC will only talk at {0}. Unless the flight controller's CAN_Px_BITRATE is set to the same speed, the ESC drops off the bus: no throttle, no telemetry, and this app cannot reach it to change it back. Some ESCs apply it only after a power cycle.

data.name: Warn_Rate1
data.value: StatusMsg1 carries RPM. ArduPilot uses it for ESC RPM telemetry and the RPM-based harmonic notch; a low rate or Off degrades that.

data.name: Warn_Rate2
data.value: StatusMsg2 carries voltage, current and temperature used by ArduPilot's ESC telemetry.

data.name: Warn_Rate3
data.value: StatusMsg3 carries MOSFET / capacitor / motor temperatures (ArduPilot does not use it).

data.name: Tip_ArduPilotHelp
data.value: How to set up ArduPilot for Hobbywing ESCs on CAN

data.name: Help_Title
data.value: ArduPilot setup for ESCs on CAN

data.name: Help_Intro
data.value: Connect the ESCs in a chain to the CAN1 (or CAN2) port of the flight controller and put a terminator on the last one. Then set the parameters below in Mission Planner (Config → Full Parameter List). The examples are for port CAN1 and driver 1.

data.name: Help_Driver
data.value: Driver 1 on port CAN1. For port CAN2: CAN_P2_DRIVER = 1 (and «FC CAN bus» = 2 in this app).

data.name: Help_Bitrate
data.value: Bus speed; must be the same as «CAN speed» of every ESC. Hobbywing ESCs come from the factory at 500000: for the first setup set 500000 here, change the ESCs to 1 Mbit/s, then set 1000000 back.

data.name: Help_EscBm
data.value: Outputs (SERVOn) sent to the ESCs over CAN, bit 0 = output 1: 15 = outputs 1–4, 63 = 1–6, 255 = 1–8.

data.name: Help_Option
data.value: Bit 7 «HobbyWingESC»: ArduPilot takes RPM, voltage, current and temperature from the Hobbywing messages (StatusMsg1/2) and asks the ESCs for their throttle channels. Add 128 to the current value.

data.name: Help_EscOf
data.value: Only when the motors do not start from output 1: e.g. motors on outputs 5–8 → 4 (ESC_BM = 240), and the ESC on output 5 gets throttle channel 1.

data.name: Help_EscRv
data.value: Only for reversible (3D) ESCs, a bitmask like ESC_BM. Usually 0.

data.name: Help_Node
data.value: Node ID of the flight controller itself (10 by default). The ESCs and this app («App node ID») must use other IDs.

data.name: Help_ServoFunction
data.value: Motor1 = 33, Motor2 = 34, … on the motor outputs; FRAME_CLASS / FRAME_TYPE usually set them.

data.name: Help_Notch
data.value: Optional, with INS_HNTCH_ENABLE = 1: harmonic notch filter that follows the RPM of the ESCs. Needs StatusMsg1 (RPM) from every ESC.

data.name: Help_Reboot
data.value: Reboot the flight controller after changing the CAN_* parameters.

data.name: Help_EscText
data.value: • CAN speed = CAN_P1_BITRATE. • Throttle source = CAN: in PWM mode the ESC ignores the throttle from ArduPilot. • Throttle channel = number of the output (SERVOn) of this motor, minus CAN_D1_UC_ESC_OF. • Node ID: unique on the bus, usually the same as the throttle channel. • StatusMsg1 rate (RPM) higher than StatusMsg2 rate. • From the factory every ESC has node ID 1 and throttle channel 1. Set them up one at a time with only one ESC on CAN: X8 G2 applies a new node ID / throttle channel to every ESC on the bus.

data.name: Help_AppText
data.value: • ArduPilot 4.3 or newer (MAV_CMD_CAN_FORWARD). • «FC CAN bus» = number of the CAN port the ESCs are on (1 = CAN_P1). • «App node ID» is free on the bus. • Connect over USB: a 57600 telemetry radio is too slow for CAN forwarding.

data.name: Help_CheckText
data.value: Props off! Mission Planner → Setup → Optional Hardware → Motor Test: every motor spins in its turn and in the right direction. RPM, voltage and current of every ESC appear on the Status tab of Mission Planner and in the «ArduPilot ESC telemetry» table of this app.
